messages:
anna_support: FYI escalation from Acme. Customer uses JSON mode + streaming to emit an array of objects. They report frequent truncated/invalid JSON mid-stream, usually after some idle heartbeats. here are the bits they sent and a minimal curl they used. request id: r-1234.

Customer payload sample (truncated):
{"items":[{"id":"1","text":"hello"},{"id":"2","text":"incomplete"}

curl they used:
curl -v "https://api.redwoodai.com/v1/generate" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-cus-..." \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -H "x-request-id: r-1234" \n  -d '{"mode":"json_stream","prompt":"...","max_tokens":2048}'

liam_sre: thanks anna. do we have tcp/edge logs for r-1234? which region and which edge (cf/nginx/lb)? any evidence of 401/429 midstream?

anna_support: customer says it started after they enabled keepalive heartbeats in their client lib. They saw a final chunk that is basically a CRLF heartbeat and then the stream ends. No 401/429 from their point of view. Region: eu-west-1. Path shows CF edge -> alb -> nginx-ingress -> runtime.

raj_ingress: fyi elastic_deploy_bot reported a small config roll earlier in eu-west at 2026-03-12 that touched proxy timeouts (roll id: deploy-981). Could be related. From past incidents, if a proxy sends an immediate FIN on an idle keepalive probe, the client sees the TCP close before the final SSE event completes which leaves JSON half-written.

liam_sre: can you paste the end of the SSE stream? what does the last bytes look like on the wire? even a hex dump helps. we need to know if the last chunk ended mid-token or if a CRLF was injected.

anna_support: customer provided the last bytes (hexdump):
0000  7b 22 69 74 65 6d 73 22 3a 5b 7b 22 69 64 22 3a 22 31  {"items":[{"id":"1
0012  22 2c 22 74 65 78 74 22 3a 22 68 65 6c 6c 6f 22 7d  ","text":"hello"}
0024  2c 7b 22 69 64 22 3a 22 32 22 2c 22 74 65 78 74 22  ,{"id":"2","text"
0036  3a 22 69 6e 63 6f 6d 70 6c 65                        :"incomplete"

so final bytes cut off after the string 'incomplete' without the closing quotes/braces.

raj_ingress: that exact pattern matches a FIN mid-write. Possible culprits: cloud edge timeout, nginx proxy_buffering + proxy_next_upstream_timeout, or LB healthcheck interfering. Also would explain why it correlates with heartbeat enable — heartbeats keep the TCP connection alive but some proxy may interpret long idle data flow differently and force-close.

liam_sre: repro plan -> we need a minimal reproducer that streams an SSE JSON array and injects a heartbeat pause. if we can reproduce internally we can rule out customer SDK. can you try this curl -> emulate small chunks + pause:

# reproduction (server):
# netcat that sends two chunks then sleeps then exits
(echo -e "data: {\"items\":[{\"id\":\"1\",\"text\":\"ok\"}] }\n\n"; sleep 2; echo -e "data: ,{\"id\":\"2\",\"text\":\"incomplete\"}" ) | nc -l 18000

# client: 
curl -v http://localhost:18000/ -H "Accept: text/event-stream" --no-buffer

anna_support: doing that now on a sandbox in eu-west. also asked customer to capture tcpdump if possible. they said they saw a FIN right after a 2 byte keepalive payload.

elastic_deploy_bot: deploy-981 (nginx-ingress config) rolled at 2026-03-12T03:14Z in eu-west-1; changed proxy_read_timeout from 90 -> 30s (note)

anna_support: ah that looks like it could explain it. they were streaming for >30s with heartbeats every 15s; the proxy timeout being 30s might close mid-event when combined with timing race.

raj_ingress: short-term mitigations:
- ask customer to set heartbeat interval to <15s or disable streaming heartbeats (client-side)
- set SDK option to treat stream data as newline-delimited JSON events (safe parse) instead of assuming a single array atomic write
- for us: bump proxy_read_timeout on ingress or enable proxy_send_timeout handling for streaming endpoints

liam_sre: longer term: eng-runtime should harden SSE emission to write final object + trailing newline/terminator in a single syscall where possible. also add server-side sentinel event like `data: __STREAM_END__` before closing to ensure client parser knows stream ended gracefully.

anna_support: customer tried disabling client heartbeats and reported fewer truncations but still one occurrence. asked them for tcpdump; they uploaded pcap and it shows FIN from ALB 10.0.3.12 at 11:02:15. request id r-1234 maps to that connection.

liam_sre: next actions:
- ops to correlate ALB logs for that timestamp and confirm if ALB timed out or actively closed. (ops: please attach logs)
- ingress to review deploy-981 and consider reverting proxy_read_timeout change for streaming routes or add a specific location rule to keep timeouts higher
- support to send customer a reproducible curl and Node snippet to aggregate chunks client-side while we investigate

anna_support: sharing Node snippet to aggregate: 
```js
const res = await fetch(url, {headers:{Accept: 'text/event-stream'}})
const reader = res.body.getReader()
let buf = ''
while(true){
  const {value, done} = await reader.read()
  if(done) break
  buf += new TextDecoder().decode(value)
  try{
    // attempt parse only when buffer looks like complete JSON (very simple heuristic)
    if(buf.trim().endsWith('}')){
      const parsed = JSON.parse(buf)
      // handle parsed
      buf = ''
    }
  }catch(e){
    // wait for more data
  }
}
```

customer_jira_bot: Created JIRA INC-4521 for customer Acme (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4521) - assigned to eng-runtime, priority P1

liam_sre: good. please attach pcap, ALB access log, and the customer's client SDK version. if we can reproduce with our netcat + ALB in front we can escalate to runtime.

raj_ingress: I'll open a rollback PR to revert deploy-981 changes for streaming endpoints and add specific ingress annotations: proxy_read_timeout: 90s for /v1/generate and /v1/stream routes.

anna_support: customer is ok with temporary workaround on their end and wants us to confirm root cause. I'll keep them updated. tagging eng-runtime: @raj_ingress please ping when PR merged so I can relay to customer. :eyes:

liam_sre: thanks all. adding note: also verify billing/auth: if a token refresh occurs midstream we sometimes see client re-try semantics that can interleave causing parse errors — check auth logs for any 401 around r-1234 as a secondary root cause.

(END)
